name: QuickBooks App Per Company
description: QuickBooks App Per Company describes a customer-managed Intuit OAuth client dedicated by policy to one QuickBooks Online company, even though Intuit binds each authorization to a selected company realm rather than requiring one app per company.
agentUseSummary: This dedicated-client deployment pattern is visible as a canonical QuickBooks extension preview. Relay will not collect Intuit app secrets or create parallel accounting tools beside the exact-realm canonical connector.

capabilities.label: Use a customer-managed QuickBooks app
capabilities.description: If this identity mode is approved, extend the canonical QuickBooks connector with immutable app, environment and exact-company realm binding while retaining only its three bounded read tools.

blocked.label: Create duplicate QuickBooks provider state
blocked.description: A per-company app listing must not create parallel company tokens, tools or approvals beside Relay's canonical QuickBooks connector.

blocked.label: Capture customer-managed Intuit credentials
blocked.description: Relay will not ask an operator to paste an Intuit app client secret, authorization code, access token or refresh token into this Marketplace alias.

blocked.label: Administer an Intuit app
blocked.description: Creating apps, completing production questionnaires, registering redirects, rotating keys and changing app settings remain Intuit developer-console workflows.

blocked.label: Relax company or scope binding
blocked.description: Relay will not substitute a realm, reuse one company's token for another, broaden accounting access or mix sandbox and production credentials.

blocked.label: Run QuickBooks actions from the setup alias
blocked.description: This alias exposes no runtime actions; approved customer-managed identity must extend the canonical connector with immutable app, environment and company-realm binding.

approvalProfiles.label: QuickBooks customer-managed app security review
approvalProfiles.description: This accounting identity alias is not connectable. Customer-managed Intuit credentials remain unavailable until Relay can enforce exact realm, environment, secret, token and revocation boundaries safely.

runtimeSupport.description: This alias installs no OpenClaw tools; approved customer-managed identity must extend the canonical QuickBooks provider pack.
This alias installs no Hermes tools; approved customer-managed identity must extend the canonical QuickBooks provider pack.

providerSetup.blocker: Intuit creates client credentials per app and separate development and production credential sets. During OAuth the user selects a QuickBooks Online company, and the resulting authorization code and tokens are bound to that company's realmId. Intuit supports one app managing multiple exact realm connections; a separate customer-managed app per company is a deployment choice, not a distinct provider connection type, and Relay's canonical connector currently uses a reviewed Relay-owned app.
providerSetup.nextAction: Prefer the Relay-owned canonical QuickBooks connector and create a distinct exact-realm connection for each company. If customer-managed apps are approved, extend that connector with immutable client, environment and realmId binding; exact callback and state validation; encrypted secret storage; rolling refresh-token replacement; revocation; sandbox/production isolation; and the existing three redacted read tools. Never create parallel alias tools or accept pasted tokens.

evidence.supports: Intuit documents one registered app initiating user consent and receiving an authorization code plus realmId that identifies the exact selected QuickBooks Online company.
Intuit requires apps to map multiple company connections by each unique realmId and recommends multiple-company support for users and accountants.
Intuit's OAuth company selector can present multiple QuickBooks companies available to one user; the selected company is the authorization boundary.
Intuit issues unique client credentials per app with distinct development and production sets, and production credentials require questionnaire approval.
